lawyer:

full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J : This Criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.9-2015, passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17827 of 2008, dis-charging the Rule and directing the trial Court to proceed with the case in accordance with law. 

 3. Under such circumstances, the Board in its 45th meeting decided to float tender afresh. The Chairman, Petrobangla, accordingly requested the Ministry of Energy for retender. But the ministry refused the same. Ultimately a committee, headed by the then State Minister for Energy Mr AKM Mosharraf Hossain, recommended to execute the contract with CMC Consortium and placed such proposal to the Cabinet Purchase Committee at the behest of the Ministry of Energy. The accused petitioner, being the head of that committee, accepted such proposal, ignoring the recommendation for re-tender and thereby allowed the CMC Consortium to make a pecuniary benefit to the tune of Taka 158 crores of public money. The accused petitioner, thereby, committed an offence punishable under sections 409/406/409/419/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. Hence the case. 

 4. The Anti-Corruption Commission then took up the matter and after inquiry Lodged an ejahar entrusting Monirul Haque, one of the Deputy Directors to investigate the case. On completion of investigation the said Deputy Director submitted final report with recommendation to discharge all the accused-persons from the allegations with observation that, no prima facie case was found to be established against any of them. 

 5. Subsequently on further investigation, Abul Kashem Fakir, the Investigating Officer, found prima facie case against the FIR named accused persons including the accused petitioner under sections 409/406/109/419/420 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and accordingly submitted charge sheet against all the accused persons recommending them for trial for misappropriation of public money by misusing official power in connivance with each other. 

 7. In the meantime, on 28-8-2008, the present petitioner obtained bail from the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 14983 of 2008 filed under section 498 of the Criminal Procedure Code. 

 8. Thereafter, this accused-petitioner again moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Criminal Procedure Code in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 17827 of 2008 for quashing the aforesaid proceeding, on several grounds including those of violation of the provisions of section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 read with rule 15(2) of the দুর্নীতি দমন কমিশন বিধিমালা-২০০৭ and thereby obtained Rule and stay. Ultimately the said Rule has been discharged by a Division Bench of the High Court Division with direction as stated above by the impugned judgment and order dated 17-9-2015. 

 10. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner submits that the present case initiated against the petitioner being abuse of the process of the court should have been quashed but the High Court Division having not done so the impugned judgment- and order is liable to be set aside. He submits that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the earlier investigating officer having not found any prima facie case against the petitioner submitted final report and, as such, submission of the charge sheet by the subsequent investigating officer, upon implicating the present petitioner, intentionally, is without any basis; that the entire action in respect of the contract has been done in accordance with the Rules of Business of the government, which falls with the policy decision of the Government, submission of the charge sheet against her is without any lawful authority as the same is based on hypothetical grounds. According to Mr Ahmed the words used in the FIR as well as in the charge sheet that “ ক্ষতি সাধনের মাধ্যমে আত্মসাৎ করেছেন ” clearly indicates loss or damage which cannot be termed as misappropriation. Moreover admittedly there being no irregularity in the evaluation process of bids the allegation of “ ক্ষতি সাধনের মাধ্যমে আত্মসাৎ করেছেন ” does not arise at all and, as such, the same does not fall within the purview of sections 409/109 of the Penal Code or section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947. He next submits that in the absence of obtaining prior sanction under section 32(1) of the Act read with Rule 13(2) of the ACC Rules 2007 before taking cognizance of any offence under the aforementioned provisions of law the instant proceeding is unlawful and, as such, the same is nothing but abuse of the process of the court. He lastly submits that no offence under section 409 of the Penal Code has been constituted by the petitioner since there is no entrustment and, as such, there is no question of any criminal breach of trust. Thus the High Court Division, committed illegality in discharging the Rule by the impugned judgment which is liable to be set aside. 

 12. Considering the submissions of the learned Counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the FIR, Police Report and the sanction order, as required under section 32 of the ACC Act 2004 read with Rule 15(2) of the Bidhimala, 2007 it appears that admittedly the accused petitioner was the then Prime Minister of the People's Republic of Bangladesh who accorded approval as the head of the final authority to issue work-order in favour of CMC consortium, the third lowest among the three bidders, inspite of recommendation of the Chairman, Petro Bangla for re-tender which according to the respondents has caused huge loss and damage to the Public Exchequer as the same constitute criminal breach of trust, punishable under section 409 of the penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1947. Thus the case has been filed by the respondents which according to the petitioner should be quashed under section 561A of the Criminal Procedure Code. But the High Court Division refused such prayer of the accused petitioner. Hence this criminal petition for leave to appeal has been filed by the petitioner. 

 13. For quashing a proceeding under section 561A of the Code, the High Court Division has scope only to see whether there are materials on record showing that the allegations made in the FIR and the charge sheet, constitute an offence. If there be any such material the proceeding shall not be quashed, in that case the trial Court will decide the case on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties in the case. 

 14. On this point, this Division in the case of Ali Akkas vs Enayet Hossain, reported in 17 BLD (AD) 44 = 2 BLC (AD) 16 held to bring a case within the purview of section 561A of the Code for the purpose of quashing a proceeding, one of the following conditions must be fulfilled: 

 (I) Interference even at an initial stage may be justified where the facts are so preposterous that even on admitted facts no case stands against the accused; 

 (IV) In a case where the allegations in the FIR or the petition of complaint, even if taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not constitute the offence alleged and . 

 (V) The allegations against the accused although constitute an offence alleged but there is either no legal evidence adduced in support of the case or the evidence adduced clearly or manifestly fails to prove the charge.’ 

 15. On perusal of the statements made in the FIR and the charge sheet it appears that there are some materials which may constitute offence punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 considering which the High Court Division held that there is clear and strong prima facie case of dishonest misappropriation of public property or otherwise disposal of public property in violation of law constituting offence punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947'. 

 16. The learned Counsel for the petitioner could not make out any case, on the basis of the facts and circumstances stated above, which could attract either of the conditions as laid down in the aforesaid decision. Thus the petitioner cannot get any remedy under section 561A of the Code. 

 17. It further appears from memo dated 5-10-2008 (Annexure-E) that the sanction for filing charge sheet has been granted on the basis of which the investigating officer submitted the charge sheet and the Court took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner and, as such, the submission of the learned counsel that 'there is no prior sanction in this case has no basis.
